P1: The RTX PRO 6000 queue has the most free capacity, but it needs recent software. In one measurement, 58 of its 64 GPUs were idle while the A100 queue had 900 jobs pending against 10 free GPUs. The queue is idle because the card is sm_120, and the PyTorch builds in the conda environments include precompiled kernels only up to sm_90. Code still runs, because the driver JIT-compiles the PTX at load time, but nothing is precompiled for this card. On a small fp32 CNN, this cost a one-time JIT delay of about 85 s. After that, steady-state speed was about 5% slower than A100. The queue is fine for single-GPU work. It has no NVLink or InfiniBand, so do not use it for multi-GPU or multi-node jobs.
P2: By default, Slack messages always go to the user. When asked to "send a Slack message", "draft a message", or something similar, send or draft it as a DM to the user so they can review it and forward it. Never send a message directly to another person or to a channel unless the user explicitly says "send to <person>" or "post in <channel>". Even then, confirm with the user before sending.
P3: Never install packages into a conda env while a cluster job that uses that env is running. Check `bjobs` first. If such a job is running, either wait for it to finish or run `mamba create -n <env>_v2 --clone <env>` and install into the clone. pip can silently replace packages such as numpy or scipy on disk while a Python process is using them. Modules the process has already imported stay in memory, but any module it imports later may load the new version. After any change to an env, immediately run `pip freeze > env/<name>_pinned_requirements.txt` and record the date, so that results can be traced to a known set of packages.
P4: When I say "upload to Google Drive" for a .pptx, .docx, .pdf, or .html deliverable and give no folder, upload to the team deliverables folder through the rclone remote `drive:` with `--drive-root-folder-id <ID>`. Before uploading, list the folder and check for a file with the same name. Do not overwrite someone else's file. Put all the files in one local staging folder and run `rclone copy` once on that folder. Then verify the upload with `rclone check --checksum --one-way <stage> drive: --drive-root-folder-id <ID>` and report how many files matched. Never verify with `--size-only`.
P5: Codex sends the prompt and every file it reads to OpenAI. This is fine for the user's own analyses. Ask the user before sending patient data, embargoed collaborator data, or anything the user has marked as sensitive. Verify every Codex finding before you apply it.
